subject: SLA template: exception playbook, credit escrow & latency routing

Subject: Initial ask: SLA template + exception handling for maintenance/credits

Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stratify's engineering and ops teams were impressed with the routing controls and batching recommendations. We’re in parallel moving the legal/procurement review, and they’ve asked for a single-statement SLA template we can use as a baseline. A couple items they want spelled out explicitly before procurement proceeds:  

- A clear exception playbook for planned maintenance windows vs emergent platform incidents (we need fields for notice periods and maximum monthly maintenance minutes carved out).
- How monthly service credits would be calculated and whether credits can be escrowed/held for multi-month outages (we have internal accounting rules that prefer escrow vs immediate offset).
- For latency-sensitive endpoints, we want to understand automatic routing to higher-capacity zones and whether that counts as an exception or a fallback (and how credits/availability are measured in that case).

I’ve attached the Stratify checklist (baseline_sla_questions.pdf) with our procurement comments — high level ask: can you send a short template + example calculation and an ops playbook for exceptions? If you prefer, we can accept a short set of redlines and then have legal adapt.

Cheers,
Alice

Director, Platform Engineering
Stratify Systems

Subject: Re: Initial ask: SLA template + exception handling for maintenance/credits

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise draft SLA template (proposed_sla_redline.pdf) and an internal playbook sketch for exception handling. High-level responses below and then a few questions so we can align the language for procurement:  

1) Planned maintenance vs emergent incidents
- Planned maintenance: defined windows with >=72 hours notice for standard maintenance; optional urgent maintenance with >=4 hours notice and post-facto report. Planned minutes are carved out from monthly uptime calculations (we include a monthly maintenance allowance of X mins — see the template).
- Emergent incidents: measured against the full availability window and eligible for service credits where availability falls below the standard uptime percent.

2) Credit calculation and escrow
- Credits are calculated monthly as a percentage of monthly service fees, tiered by severity and aggregate minutes lost. We can support an escrow mechanism for credits (held for up to 6 months) before auto-applying them to invoices — requires a short addendum to enable escrow accounting (we included sample language).

3) Latency-sensitive routing / fallback
- Automatic routing to higher-capacity zones is treated as a resilience measure; availability for the routed request is measured end-to-end. If routing results in higher latency for a subset of requests we treat that as a degraded performance incident (latency SLO trigger) rather than an availability outage; credits for latency degradations are calculated against p95/p99 thresholds specified per endpoint in the template.

Questions for procurement/legal:
- Would Stratify accept a 6-month escrow cap or do you require longer-term holding?
- Do you want routing events (cross-region fallback) to be excluded from availability calculations if Stratify elects to opt into multi-region redundancy (we can add an "opt-in redundancy carveout")?

Next steps: I’ve asked Ben (billing) to draft the escrow operations note and a sample Excel calc so your finance folks can see the monthly treatment. Laura — if you can review the maintenance notice wording and the 72h/4h split, I’ll incorporate into the redline.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: escrow calc + ops note for Stratify

Looping in with the spreadsheet and quick ops notes for escrow handling. Key points we should surface to Stratify as part of the template:  

- Escrow accounting flow: when a credit is earned in month N it is recorded as a credit token. If escrow is enabled, tokens pool in the escrow account and can be applied to invoices up to month N+5. If unused by month N+6 they either roll off (per agreement) or can be claimed via a refund request (requires a signed request).
- Monthly cap: propose a default cap of 50% of monthly services fees (to avoid large one-off offsets). We can make this configurable per-customer if procurement requests a higher cap with an executed amendment.
- Latency carveouts: propose that cross-region routing used explicitly as part of customer-enabled redundancy (i.e., Stratify turned on multi-region) qualifies for a reduced availability credit (we measure latency SLOs separately).

I attached the calc (credit_escrow_calc.xlsx) — the example rows show a 40% monthly total credit bucket across three severity bands. Suggest we include a worked example in the template (we'll insert one in the PDF).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask: SLA template + exception handling for maintenance/credits

Jonas / Ben / Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the worked example. We reviewed the redline and the escrow mechanics with our finance team:  

- We can accept a 6-month escrow window but would like a clause that allows a one-time extension to month N+9 upon mutual written agreement (procurement request).
- The 50% monthly cap is acceptable as a default; we’ll flag if legal requests higher (we may accept amendments tied to committed spend tiers).
- For latency routing: Stratify prefers that cross-region automatic fallback be treated as a resilience measure and excluded from availability calculations IF we opt into multi-region redundancy. Can you add the opt-in carveout language to the template?

If you can update the redline with the extension clause and the opt-in redundancy carveout we’ll get procurement to run the final review. Once redline is agreed, procurement will open a single purchase order and sign the SOW.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a short call if any of these items need quick alignment.

Best,
Alice Moreno
Director, Platform Engineering
Stratify Systems
